skills.name: Expand products of brackets, including the special products

note.text:
To expand a product of brackets, multiply every term in one bracket by every term in the other, then collect like terms.
• (x + 3)(x + 5) = x² + 5x + 3x + 15 = x² + 8x + 15.
• (2x + 3)(x − 4) = 2x² − 8x + 3x − 12 = 2x² − 5x − 12.
Three special products are worth knowing by heart:
• (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²
• (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²
• (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²
A common mistake is (x + 3)² = x² + 9: the middle term 2 × 3 × x = 6x is missing.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to expand any product of two brackets and spot the three special products on sight.
Builds on: Form Three expansion of a(b + c) and of (x + a)(x + b); collecting like terms.
Leads to: factorisation (the next lessons undo expansion) and solving quadratic equations.

sections.heading: Every term times every term
Three special products
sections.text:
Some products appear so often that it is worth knowing them by heart.
• (a + b)² = a² + {2}ab + b²: for example ({poly([1, 'x'], [5, ''])})² = {quad(1, 10, 25)}.
• (a − b)² = a² − {2}ab + b²: for example ({poly([1, 'x'], [-3, ''])})² = {quad(1, -6, 9)}.
• (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²: for example {lin2(1, 7, 1, -7)} = {quad(1, 0, -49)}.
In the last one the middle terms cancel. This is called the difference of two squares, and the next lesson uses it backwards.

key_words.meaning: remove the brackets by multiplying every term inside
a bracket times itself, such as ({poly([1, 'x'], [5, ''])})²
an expression a² − b², which equals (a + b)(a − b)

mistake.why: Squaring a bracket means multiplying it by itself. The two middle products {mono(3, 'x')} + {mono(3, 'x')} give {mono(6, 'x')}.

worked_example.problem: Expand and simplify {lin2(a, b, c, d)}.
steps: Multiply each term of the first bracket by each term of the second.
Collect the x terms: {a * d} + {b * c} = {a * d + b * c}.
worked_example.answer: {quad(a * c, a * d + b * c, b * d)}

cards.idea: Every term in one bracket multiplies every term in the other. Two terms times two terms make four products.
A square of a bracket is the bracket times itself, so it has a middle term: twice the product of the two terms.
When the brackets differ only by a sign, the middle terms cancel: the answer is a difference of two squares.

misconceptions.explain: The last product is {q} × {br(-q)}: a positive times a negative is negative, so {-q * q}.
The middle products are {mono(-p * q, 'x')} and {mono(p * q, 'x')}: they cancel to zero.

solution: The middle products are {mono(-p * q, 'x')} and {mono(p * q, 'x')}: they cancel.

misconceptions.explain: Two products are missing: x × {br(q)} and {br(p)} × x. Together they give {mono(p + q, 'x')}.
The last term is a product: {br(p)} × {br(q)} = {p * q}, not a sum.
The x term comes from adding: {p} + {br(q)} = {p + q}. The number term comes from multiplying: {p * q}.

solution: x × x = x²; x × {br(q)} and {br(p)} × x give {p} + {br(q)} = {p + q} lots of x.

questions.prompt: Expand {lin2(1, a, 1, a)}, that is ({poly([1, 'x'], [a, ''])})². What is the coefficient of x?

misconceptions.explain: There are two middle products, x × {br(a)} and {br(a)} × x: {a} + {br(a)} = {2 * a}.
{a * a} is the number term ({br(a)} × {br(a)}). The x term is {2 * a}x.

solution: The two middle products are {br(a)} × x and x × {br(a)}: together {mono(2 * a, 'x')}.
So the coefficient of x is {answer}.

questions.prompt: Expand and simplify {lin2(a, b, c, d)}.
questions.correct: {quad(a * c, a * d + b * c, b * d)}

distractors.text: {quad(a * c, a * b + c * d, b * d)}
{quad(a + c, a * d + b * c, b + d)}

misconceptions.explain: Multiply a term of the first bracket by a term of the second: {mono(a, 'x')} × {br(d)} and {b} × {mono(c, 'x')}.
The two middle products are missing: {mono(a * d, 'x')} and {mono(b * c, 'x')}.
Terms are multiplied, not added: {mono(a, 'x')} × {mono(c, 'x')} = {mono(a * c, 'x²')} and {b} × {br(d)} = {b * d}.

solution: Middle: {mono(a, 'x')} × {br(d)} + {b} × {mono(c, 'x')} = {mono(a * d, 'x')} + {mono(b * c, 'x')} = {mono(a * d + b * c, 'x')}.
where: a * b + c * d != a * d + b * c

misconceptions.explain: The last product is {q} × {br(-q)}: a positive times a negative is negative, so {-q * q}.
The middle products are {mono(-p * q, 'x')} and {mono(p * q, 'x')}: they cancel to zero.

solution: The middle products are {mono(-p * q, 'x')} and {mono(p * q, 'x')}: they cancel.

questions.prompt: Expand ({poly([1, 'x'], [a, ''])})({quad(1, b, c)}). What is the coefficient of x?

misconceptions.explain: There is a second x term: {br(a)} × {mono(b, 'x')} = {mono(a * b, 'x')}.
There is a second x term: x × {br(c)} = {mono(c, 'x')}.
{b} + {br(a)} is the coefficient of x². For x add {c} and {a} × {br(b)}.

solution: The x terms come from x × {br(c)} and {br(a)} × {mono(b, 'x')}.
So the coefficient of x is {c} + {br(a * b)} = {answer}.
